english: you can’t have it both ways
also: you can’t do two things at once
you can’t be in two places at once
you can’t have your cake and eat it
you can’t whistle and drink at the same time

terms.latin: Simul flāre sorbēreque haud factū facile est.
terms.gloss: it is not easy to blow and sup at the same time
evidence: Plaut. Most. 791: simul flāre sorbēreque haud factū facilest
terms.comment: Of doing two opposite things at once (Lewis & Short s.v. sorbeō). The slave who says it explains: he could not be here and there together.

phrases.latin: simul flāre sorbēreque haud factū facilest. Ego hīc esse et illīc simitū hau potuī.
phrases.english: blowing and supping at the same time is no easy thing to do. I couldn’t be here and there at once.
